## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

v5.0.0

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING]
The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

v5.0.0

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING]
The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING] The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING]
The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

v5.0.0

v5 Release

v5 of the Codecov GitHub Action will use the Codecov Wrapper to encapsulate the CLI. This will help ensure that the Action gets updates quicker.

Migration Guide

The v5 release also coincides with the opt-out feature for tokens for public repositories. In the Global Upload Token section of the settings page of an organization in codecov.io, you can set the ability for Codecov to receive a coverage reports from any source. This will allow contributors or other members of a repository to upload without needing access to the Codecov token. For more details see how to upload without a token.

[!WARNING]
The following arguments have been changed

  • file (this has been deprecated in favor of files)
  • plugin (this has been deprecated in favor of plugins)

The following arguments have been added:

  • binary
  • gcov_args
  • gcov_executable
  • gcov_ignore
  • gcov_include
  • report_type
  • skip_validation
  • swift_project

You can see their usage in the action.yml file.

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function

Some of it is more controversial than others so I'm happy to remove some parts or move things to other parts as needed. Overall, my aim has been to make the API closer to that of `GenericMap` but with an added dimension. 

Summary of changes below:

- Deprecate the `derotate` keyword. As far as I can tell, this has never actually done anything. 
- Refactor logic of how sort-by methods are selected. This is all internal
- Deprecate the `resample` kwarg in `plot`. This is a separation-of-concerns issue. Why should `plot` be doing any resampling? If you want to plot a resampled map, resample it yourself first.
- Deprecate `resample` in `peek`. See above.
- Do not allow for non-WCS axes to be passed to `plot`. We've not allowed this on `Map` for a long time. I'm not even sure it would work here. I've not deprecated this because I consider it undocumented behavior to begin with.
- Deprecate the method `all_maps_same_shape`. I don't see any need for this to be part of the public API. 
- Deprecate the method `at_least_one_map_has_mask`. Same as above.
- Deprecate the method `as_array` in favor of the new properties `data` and `mask`. Previously, `as_array` returned a masked array if at least one map held a mask and a bare array if not. This refactor now separates these properties similar to how `GenericMap` treats them
- Deprecate the method `all_meta` in favor of the new property `meta`

My aim was to deprecate things rather than remove them outright as that would constitute a breaking change. However, if there's no opposition, I'm also happy to outright break things. PR does a bunch of miscellaneous cleanup on `MapSequence`. Some of it is more controversial than others so I'm happy to remove some parts or move things to other parts as needed. Overall, my aim has been to make the API closer to that of `GenericMap` but with an added dimension. 

Summary of changes below:

- Deprecate the `derotate` keyword. As far as I can tell, this has never actually done anything. 
- Refactor logic of how sort-by methods are selected. This is all internal
- Deprecate the `resample` kwarg in `plot`. This is a separation-of-concerns issue. Why should `plot` be doing any resampling? If you want to plot a resampled map, resample it yourself first.
- Deprecate `resample` in `peek`. See above.
- Do not allow for non-WCS axes to be passed to `plot`. We've not allowed this on `Map` for a long time. I'm not even sure it would work here. I've not deprecated this because I consider it undocumented behavior to begin with.
- Deprecate the method `all_maps_same_shape`. I don't see any need for this to be part of the public API. 
- Deprecate the method `at_least_one_map_has_mask`. Same as above.
- Deprecate the method `as_array` in favor of the new properties `data` and `mask`. Previously, `as_array` returned a masked array if at least one map held a mask and a bare array if not. This refactor now separates these properties similar to how `GenericMap` treats them
- Deprecate the method `all_meta` in favor of the new property `meta`

My aim was to deprecate things rather than remove them outright as that would constitute a breaking change. However, if there's no opposition, I'm also happy to outright break things. comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description
Fixes #6382 
Before applying `plot_settings` 
```
comp_map = sunpy.map.Map(aia_smap, hmi_smap, composite=True)
levels = [-1000, -500, -250, 250, 500, 1000] * u.G
comp_map.set_levels(index=1, levels=levels)

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```
Edit: I just realised the image below is not what is used to, this needs to be fixed
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26901c77-0471-449d-98d1-b5a24d32ac5f)
After adding `plot_settings`
```
settings1 = comp_map.get_plot_settings(1)

settings1['linewidths'] = 4
settings1['alpha'] = 1
settings1['zorder'] = 10
fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection=comp_map.get_map(0))
comp_map.plot(axes=ax)
plt.show()
```

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

PR Description

Adds ability in Map and Timeseries factories to recognize and parse URI paths. It was designed with s3 paths in mind but would work for any type of URI. If path is a URI, it will use the `fsspec` package to open, read, and look for files.

#### Example code:
```
### Reads in fits file from public s3 repository using anonymous credentials
from sunpy.map import Map
Map("s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/sdo/aia/20100513/0131/sdo_aia_h2_20100513T000400_0131_v1.fits", fsspec_kwargs={'anon': True})

### Reads in cdf file from public s3 repository (REQUIRES VALID AWS CREDENTIALS AND SETUP)
from sunpy.timeseries import TimeSeries
TimeSeries('s3://gov-nasa-hdrl-data1/cdaweb/ace/mag/level_2_cdaweb/mfi_k2/2017/ac_k2_mfi_20170705_v03.cdf')
```

#### Descriptions to changes in code:

- `Pyproject.toml` - adds `fsspec` as package dependency; adds `s3fs` as test dependency.
- `sunpy/io/_cdf.py` - passes kwargs to reader function.
- `Sunpy/io/_filetools.py` - adds way to open URI filetype using `fsspec.open` to `detect_filetype`
- `Sunpy/map/map_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using `parse_uri` function
- `sunpy/map/tests/test_map_factory.py` - adds unit test to read map from s3 public repository.
- `sunpy/timeseries/tests/test_timeseries_factory.py` - adds unit test to read timeseries from s3 public repository; will skip if credentials/permissions are incorrect.
- `Sunpy/timeseries/timeseries_factory.py` - adds logic to separate URI file path from regular filepath and parses URIs using parse_uri function; refactors previous code for parsing timeseries results into separate function.
- `Sunpy/util/io.py` 
  - `parse_uri` - reads in a list of fsspec OpenFile objects; follows same structure as parse_path
  - `is_uri` - function to recognize URI objects; code taken from `pandas`

Happy to iterate or discuss further on methodology.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

If we want to do it by area we have to do a little bit of shenanigans with sorted arrays, like [in this gist](https://gist.github.com/settwi/5d3f34b79843df00c2058ec1d49da2ea). We could extend the example to N-dimensions, too.

This would be a pretty small addition to the contour code but probably make people happy!

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

![Screenshot 2024-11-29 103728](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d537f64-3cf0-4385-9604-c206bff90179)

This fixes #77

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.

## PR Description

**Function Signature Update:**

Changed ccd_temperature=-60.0 to ccd_temperature=-60.0 * u.deg_C.

**Temperature Handling:**

Added a check to ensure ccd_temperature is an Astropy Quantity.

Converted non-Quantity inputs to u.deg_C.

Ensured temperature is in degrees Celsius for consistency.

**Gain Interpolation:**

Used temp_x values directly (assumed in degrees Celsius).

Used .value to get numerical values for interpolation.

**Docstring Update:**

Described ccd_temperature as an Astropy Quantity with units.

**Testing:**

The function now accepts both Quantity and float inputs for temperature.

Temperatures provided in different units are converted to degrees Celsius.
